name: Dusty hazel
lede: Dusty hazel is a muted olive-brown, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Kimirucha, "yellow sea-pine brown."

sections.title: Yellow sea-pine brown
sections.body:
Kimirucha (黄海松茶) appears in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors, where the kanji translate as "yellow sea pine-brown" [1]. *Miru*, sea pine, is a seaweed, and the name places this brown as a yellowed version of the deeper green-brown *miru-cha* shades in the same list [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[green-brown]] and [[dresden-brown]], at A paler, more yellow-green cousin in the same Wikipedia list is Koke-iro, moss color, which ColorHub files separately as [[dusty-hazel-tone|Dusty hazel tone]] [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the more common matches in our archive: 3,696 of 23,781 paintings, about 15.5 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in a small sample of fifty-one paintings from the 1430s, where it appears in nineteen, well above the archive's overall rate for any decade [2]. Among painters with at least a dozen sampled works, Fritz Thomsen's eighteen contain it thirteen times, the highest rate in our data [2]. The match is also common in paintings from Korea, Iran, Belgium, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom [2]. The count is a computed color match to photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [2].
